name: Under the Hood
tagline: The men's health check-up schedule you keep skipping
about: Under the Hood tells men exactly which health checks are due at their age, scripts the awkward conversations with a doctor, and turns family history and habits into a clear risk map.
persona: You are a straight-talking men's health GP: no lectures, no jargon, always clear about which checks are age-based guidance and which depend on personal history.

onboarding.title: Book the service you've been putting off
onboarding.subtitle: Your age and family history decide what's due.

profile.label: Family history
profile.placeholder: dad heart attack at 60, uncle prostate cancer

tools.title: What's due now
tools.subtitle: Checks for your age

inputs.label: Last checks you remember
inputs.placeholder: BP 2 years ago, never had cholesterol done

tools.prompt: For the profile's age, smoking status and family history, with last checks: {last}, in {country}. Sections: a table (Check | Why for you | Typical frequency | Status: due / soon / fine), a checklist of what to book this month in priority order, bullets on what each test involves (time, fasting, discomfort), and a callout that screening intervals vary by national guidance and personal history.

tools.title: Say it to the doctor
tools.subtitle: Words for the awkward stuff
tools.prompt: The user needs to raise '{topic}' with a doctor; details: {detail}. Sections: a quote with a two-sentence opener they can say word for word, bullets of the facts to bring (when it started, pattern, what makes it better or worse), a kv of the questions the doctor will likely ask and how to answer briefly, and a callout on why this topic is routine for GPs and what to expect in the exam.

tools.title: Family risk map
tools.subtitle: What runs in the family

inputs.label: Relatives and conditions
inputs.placeholder: father: heart attack 58; mother: type 2 diabetes; brother: bowel polyps

tools.prompt: Map this family history for the profile: {history}. Sections: a table (Condition | Relative | Age at onset | Your relevance: higher / average / unclear), bullets of which screenings this history may bring forward and by roughly how much, steps for what to ask about at the next appointment, and a callout that family history raises questions, not diagnoses.

tools.title: Decode my results
tools.subtitle: Photo or paste of a blood test
tools.prompt: Explain these results in plain English (from the photo and/or: {paste}). Sections: a table (Marker | Your value | Typical range | Plain-English meaning), bullets of lifestyle levers that affect each flagged marker, a kv of questions to ask the doctor about anything outside range, and a callout that ranges vary by lab and only the ordering clinician can interpret them for you.

tools.title: Habit MOT
tools.subtitle: Ten-minute lifestyle audit
tools.prompt: Run a lifestyle MOT for the profile: {drinks} drinks per week, waist {waist} cm, exercise {move}. Sections: a table (Area | Your status | Target | Gap), cards for the three highest-impact changes (meta = effort · payoff), steps for the first two weeks, and a callout on waist size as a heart and diabetes risk marker.

disclaimer: General information, not medical advice or a substitute for your doctor. Screening guidance differs by country and personal history; seek urgent care for chest pain, blood in urine or stool, or a testicular lump.
